title: The Facts Concerning the Recent Carnival of Crime in Connecticut

evidence.paraphrase: A tiny deformed being suddenly enters the narrator's room.
evidence.quote:
Straightway the door opened, and a shriveled, shabby dwarf entered. He
was not more than two feet high.

evidence.paraphrase: The strange being reveals itself to be the narrator's Conscience personified.
The Conscience explains it is an unsubstantial spirit made visible only to the narrator.
evidence.quote:
No. It only made me visible to you. I am unsubstantial, just as other
spirits are.

evidence.paraphrase: The Conscience states the rule that only its owner can perceive it.
evidence.quote: For a very good reason. I am invisible to all but you.

evidence.paraphrase: The Conscience explains that its weight and position depend on the narrator's emotional state.
evidence.quote:
Otherwise it must have occurred to you that if you attempted this
murder with a sad heart and a heavy conscience, I would droop under the
burdening in influence instantly.

evidence.paraphrase: The Conscience explains its size changes over a person's life according to their conscientiousness.
evidence.quote:
When you
were eight or nine years old, I was seven feet high, and as pretty as a
picture.

evidence.paraphrase: The Conscience describes a mechanism by which repeated sinning makes it shrivel and grow callous.
evidence.quote:
The more I weakened, the more stubbornly you
fastened on to those particular sins; till at last the places on my
person that represent those vices became as callous as shark-skin.

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator deliberately formulates questions to investigate the nature of the visible Conscience.
evidence.quote:
By and by I got to musing
over the hour's strange adventure, and of course my human curiosity
began to work. I set myself to framing in my mind some questions for
this fiend to answer.

evidence.paraphrase: The Conscience explains a cooperative system among consciences to divert would-be moral pleaders.
evidence.quote:
Whenever a person whose conscience I am acquainted
with tries to plead with you about the vices you are callous to, I get
my friend to give his client a pang concerning some villainy of his
own, and that shuts off his meddling

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator reacts to learning the being's identity with joyful rage and an attempt to attack it.
evidence.quote:
In an instant I was in a blaze of joy and exultation. I sprang at the
creature, roaring:

evidence.paraphrase: Under the aunt's pleading, the Conscience is overwhelmed and falls asleep, defenseless.
evidence.quote:
With a long-drawn sigh my conquered Conscience closed his eyes
and fell fast asleep!

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator destroys and burns his Conscience.
evidence.quote:
I tore him to shreds and fragments. I rent the
fragments to bits. I cast the bleeding rubbish into the fire

evidence.paraphrase: Freed from his Conscience, the narrator commits many crimes without remorse.
evidence.quote:
I killed thirty-eight persons during the first two weeks--all of them
on account of ancient grudges. I burned a dwelling that interrupted my
view. I swindled a widow and some orphans out of their last cow

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator declares his transformed state as a man now entirely without a conscience.
evidence.quote:
You behold before you a man whose life-conflict is
done, whose soul is at peace; a man whose heart is dead to sorrow, dead
to suffering, dead to remorse; a man WITHOUT A CONSCIENCE!

evidence.paraphrase: A disproportion is drawn between a man's conscience-driven suicide and the trivial harm that provoked it.
evidence.quote:
That man walked the
floor in torture for forty-eight hours, without eating or sleeping, and
then blew his brains out. The child was perfectly well again in three
weeks.

evidence.paraphrase: A publisher's conscience is described as so tiny it required a powerful microscope to view.
evidence.quote:
The management had provided a microscope
with a magnifying power of only thirty thousand diameters, and so nobody
got to see him, after all.
